result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-166 (docs/requirements.yaml, awk-scoped read) end to end without trusting any prior step's self-report. AC-by-AC re-derivation against lib/letflow/engine/wasm/module_registry.ex (read in full) and test/letflow/engine/wasm/module_registry_test.exs (read in full): AC1 'missing execute rejected with structured error naming it' -> describe block 'AC1' (line 43) asserts {:error, {:invalid_abi, defects}} containing {:missing, "execute"}. AC2 'each other required export individually rejected' -> describe 'AC2' (line 57) has one test case per remaining required export (init, deinit, get_capabilities, alloc, memory) plus wrong-kind/wrong-signature variants. AC3 'rejection at registration, never invocation' -> describe 'AC3' (line 146): a non-conforming module never produces a registered_module() value (enforced structurally by @opaque + the module being the only construction site, confirmed by grep -- RegisteredModule{} appears nowhere outside module_registry.ex), an unresolved-import module is rejected at stage 2 before ever completing instantiation, and a stage-gating mutation-guard test proves stage 2 never runs when stage 1 already failed. AC4 'conforming module registers and is invocable' -> describe 'AC4' (line 189): returns {:ok, registered_module()} only after stage 2's real Wasmex.start_link/1 instantiation attempt actually succeeded (the module truly is invocable, not merely export-shaped), and the proving instance is confirmed not leaked via a live Wasmex-process-list diff. AC5 (moduledoc) -> module_registry.ex moduledoc cites req163-wasm-abi-choice.md sections 3.1/3.2/4 by name, lists all five required function exports plus memory, states the two-stage gate, and explicitly states core-modules-not-Components; test 'AC5' (line 338) asserts every one of these substrings is present via Code.fetch_docs/1 (not just eyeballed). AC6 (mix test / compile) -- re-run myself, not copied from TEST-RUNNER: `mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/` = 'Result: 30 passed', 0 failures (matches TEST-RUNNER's own 30). `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors` (forced full recompile, not relying on any cached build) = 'Compiling 131 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings, exit 0. Additionally re-ran the full aggregated-partition suite myself via `scripts/test_parallel.sh` as a blocking foreground call (per RELEASE-VALIDATOR's no-background-wait rule) rather than trusting TEST-RUNNER ran it minutes earlier: 8/8 partitions exit 0, combined 2313 tests + 5 properties, 0 failures (2318/2318 passed) -- independently reproduces TEST-RUNNER's exact numbers. ISS-0351 checked directly (docs/issues/ISS-0351.yaml): narrow (Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) doesn't reach the native Wasmtime dirty-NIF thread on the timeout path), severity MINOR, explicitly not yet tenant-exploitable because REQ-166 ships no tenant-facing upload/invocation path (confirmed true by reading module_registry.ex's own moduledoc 'Scope boundary' section: PluginHandler/PluginInterface are untouched), and explicitly deferred to whichever future requirement first wires a tenant-facing registration path -- none of REQ-166's own six acceptance_criteria depend on the timeout-kill's native-thread cleanup behavior, so ISS-0351 is legitimately out of scope for this requirement's gate and does not block it. Scope-creep check: `git diff --stat main...HEAD` (26 files) touches only lib/letflow/engine/wasm/module_registry.ex (new), lib/letflow/application.ex (14 lines -- re-read the diff directly: adds exactly one new sibling Task.Supervisor child per design section 2.2, nothing else changed), the req166 design doc, 11 new priv/wasm_fixtures/*.wat fixtures, the new test file, test/specs/REQ-166.md, docs/issues/ISS-0351.yaml, and this run's own handoffs/ directory -- no changes to lib/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler.ex or lib/letflow/engine/plugin_interface.ex, consistent with every prior handoff's stated non-touch and with REQ-166's own 'NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT' scope boundary (capability sandboxing/resource limits/host API/versioning all excluded). Prior gates (design validator, security reviewer, reviewer, test-design validator, test-runner) all independently re-verified rather than copied, and their own independent evidence (live test runs, live deps/wasmex source reads, live crash-propagation reproduction) is consistent with what I re-derived myself. Verdict: REQ-166's acceptance criteria are genuinely met. Cleared for DOC-UPDATER to flip docs/requirements.yaml status to done.
